persona_label: Competitive powerlifter — high BMI, elite strength

conversation_log.content:
To get us started, how would you describe your current relationship with physical movement? Are you looking to sharpen a specific blade, or are you preparing to build a completely new kind of engine?
Options: [Developing maximum explosive output and raw power | Building sustained, high-intensity aerobic capacity | Refining precision-based movement and technical efficiency]
Developing maximum explosive output and raw power

As we look toward your potential sporting journey, how do you prefer to apply that raw explosive power in a high-performance athletics context?
Options: [Heavy lifting and pure force production (e.g., weightlifting or strongman mechanics) | Dynamic, reactive acceleration (e.g., explosive starts and short-burst field dominance) | Tactical contact and physical imposition (e.g., wrestling, grappling, or combative force application)]
Heavy lifting and pure force production (e.g., weightlifting or strongman mechanics)

To better understand how we frame this pursuit, what has been your primary motivation for stepping into this intensity at this stage in your journey?
Options: [Building long-term functional power and physical resilience | Chasing the competitive edge of local and national records | Mastering the technical art and discipline of moving maximal weight]
Mastering the technical art and discipline of moving maximal weight

scouting_result.pathway_adaptive: Seated Shot Put (e.g., Men's Shot Put C3)
scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Your foundation as a master of heavy weight gives you a distinct advantage in the throwing circle. Standing at 182cm and 142kg, you possess the physical gravity that makes the shot put an extension of your own momentum. At 35, you aren't just relying on raw power; you are applying the technical precision you’ve honed through years of dedicated training, turning kinetic energy into a projectile that seems to defy physics. 

As you prepare for The 2028 Games, your focus on maximal force production transforms the shot put from a simple throw into a demonstration of total bodily control. Your stature provides the perfect fulcrum for the explosive, singular effort required at the elite level. It is here, under the lights, that your discipline for lifting heavy weight becomes your greatest weapon, allowing you to dominate the field through sheer, calculated impact.

scouting_result.pathway_adaptive: Seated Throws (e.g., Men's Discus Throw F56)
scouting_result.scout_verdict:
If your standing efforts are about overwhelming force, your adaptive pathway in seated throwing is about the mastery of isolated kinetic transfer. The F56 classification—reserved for athletes with impaired muscle power or range of movement in the lower limbs—requires a profound level of core stability and upper-body timing. Here, you cannot rely on a running start or a leg-driven pivot; instead, you must channel that same power you once used in heavy lifting into a static, high-tension environment.

At The 2028 Games, this transition to the F56 field highlights a different side of your athletic identity. By removing the legs from the equation, the sport becomes a test of extreme technical fluidity and precision. You will have to leverage every ounce of your 142kg frame through your core and shoulders, turning your sitting position into a stable launchpad. This is where your history of mastering complex weight movements truly shines, as you rewrite your biomechanical approach to generate elite-level distance without ever moving from the chair.
